Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Thermodynamics, Thermodynamics of Nucleic Acids (DNA Structure and Stability: Double-helix, Base Pairing, and Hyperchromicity, Melting of DNA: Thermodynamic Parameters (Tm, ?H, ?S), Van’t Hoff Analysis of DNA Duplex Stability, UV Absorbance and Temperature Dependence in DNA Melting), Colligative Properties and Molecular Weight Determination (Freezing Point Depression and Boiling Point Elevation, Determining Molecular Weight of Unknown Solutes via Freezing Point Depression, Calculation of Thermodynamic Parameters from Colligative Properties), Calorimetry and Heat in Biological Systems (Principles of Calorimetry, Measuring Heat Released in Biological Reactions, Coffee Cup and Bomb Calorimetry in Biological Research, Application of Calorimetry to Study Biochemical Reactions (e.g., Protein Denaturation)), Enthalpy Change in Acid-Base Reactions (Heat of Neutralization: Measurement by Thermometric Titration, Calculation of Enthalpy Change for Neutralization Reactions, Standard Enthalpy of Formation and its Role in Biological Systems), Protein Folding and Unfolding Thermodynamics (Structure and Stability of Proteins: Folding and Denaturation, Gibbs Free Energy and Protein Stability, Thermodynamics of Enzyme Reactions.

Course Objective

1 .

Understand and apply the fundamental principles of thermodynamics to biological systems.
2 .

Perform experiments to measure thermodynamic parameters such as enthalpy, free energy, and molecular weight through hands-on experiments.
3 .

To explore how thermodynamic principles relate to biological processes such as DNA stability, protein folding, and metabolic reactions.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of the course, the students will be able to:
CO1 Understand and explain basic thermodynamic concepts like energy, heat, and free energy in biological systems.
CO2 Perform experiments and analyze data to measure thermodynamic parameters in biological processes.
CO3 Calculate and interpret thermodynamic values such as melting temperature and enthalpy change for biological molecules.
CO4 Communicate experimental results through well-written lab reports demonstrating an understanding of thermodynamic principles.
CO5 Use thermodynamic principles to solve problems related to biological systems.

6912.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE4103 : Advanced Foundation Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I: Basics of Subsoil Exploration (8 hours)
Pre-requisite of a Foundation Design: Sub-surface investigation, Planning of sub-surface investigations, Execution of sub-surface investigations. Basics of Foundation Design: Shallow Foundations and Deep Foundations, Basic design criteria for Shallow Foundations and Deep Foundations.
Module II: Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations (12 hours)
Bearing capacity of Shallow Foundations: Methods for estimating the bearing capacity of Shallow Foundations under vertical, eccentric, and inclined loading in cohesionless and cohesive soils, Methods for estimating the bearing capacity of Shallow Foundations on layered soils, Methods for estimating the bearing capacity of Shallow Foundations on slopes. Settlement of Shallow Foundations: Methods for assessing the settlement of Shallow Foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils. Design of Shallow Foundations.
Module III: Bearing Capacity of Deep Foundations (12 hours)
Bearing capacity of Deep Foundations: Methods for estimating the bearing capacity of Piles and Pile groups under vertical loading in cohesionless and cohesive soils (non-expansive and expansive soils), Methods for estimating the bearing capacity of Pile groups under eccentric loading in cohesionless and cohesive soils (non-expansive and expansive soils). Settlement of Deep Foundations: Methods for assessing the settlement of Deep Foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils (non-expansive and expansive soils). Design of Deep Foundations.
Module IV: Design of Machine Foundations (4 hours)
Dynamics of Machine Foundations: Free and forced vibrations, Vibration Isolation. Design consideration for simple machine foundations under reciprocating, centrifugal, and impact-type machines.

Course Objective

1 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to have an enhanced understanding of the fundamentals of subsoil exploration.
2 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to develop the ability to design shallow foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils, including general and special cases.
3 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to develop the ability to design deep foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils, including general and special cases.
4 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to understand the basic design principles of special foundations.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, the students will be able to:
CO1: Understand the basics of Subsoil Exploration.
CO2: Design Shallow Foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils considering various general and special cases.
CO3: Design deep foundations in cohesionless and cohesive soils by considering various general and special cases.
CO4: Understand the concept of soil dynamics and machine foundation.
CO5: Design an appropriate foundation system for different types of structures.

Essential Reading

1 .

Braja M. Das and Nagaratnam Sivakugan, Principles of Foundation Engineering, Cengage Learning

2 .

Braja M. Das and G.V. Ramana, Principles of Soil Dynamics, Cengage Learning

Supplementary Reading

1 .

J. E. Bowles, Foundation Analysis and Design, Mc Graw Hill (2001)

2 .

F. H. Chen, Foundations of Expansive Soil, Elsevier Science Publisher, Amsterdam

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CR6101 : Sintering and Microstructure { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Fundamentals of high temperature processes in ceramic fabrication, processes, and properties, Defects in crystalline solids, Defect chemistry, Kroger-Vink notations, Defect equilibrium, Diffusion and driving forces, Fick’s laws, Diffusion kinetics and activation energy, diffusion types and coefficients, Chemical potential, Chemical potential of atoms and vacancies, Chemical potential of curved surfaces, Diffusional flux equation. (6 hrs)
Module 2 :

Basics of solid-state sintering, Sintering mechanisms, 3-particles model, Herring’s scaling law, Application of scaling law in various sintering mechanism, Sintering stages and microstructural features, Geometrical model for initial sintering stage, Generalized expression, Intermediate sintering stage: geometrical model and constitutive equation, Final sintering stage. (8 hrs)
Module 3 :

High temperature processes under externally applied load, Creep, Stages of creep, Constitutive model, Nabarro-Herring creep, Coble creep, Dislocation creep, Hot pressing mechanisms. (4 hrs)
Module 4 :

Liquid phase sintering: Basic features, Thermodynamic and kinetic factors, LPS additives, Examples, Dihedral angle, Wetting, penetration of grain boundaries by liquid phase, Capillary forces, Densification processes, Microstructural features, Application of phase diagram in LPS. (4 hrs)
Module 5 :

Grain growth: Basics of grain growth and coarsening, Ostwald ripening, Normal and abnormal grain growth, Boundary mobility, Burke-Turnbull model, Solute drag theory (Cahn’s model), Parabolic kinetics, Cubic kinetics, Adsorbate drag, Particle inhibited grain growth and Zener model. (6 hrs)
Module 6 :

Microstructure control: Thermodynamics of pore stability, pore mobility, Kinetics of pore-boundary interaction, Grain growth in porous systems, Brook model, Yan-Cannon-Choudhary model, Harmer model. (6 hrs)
Module 7 :

Special techniques: Use of dopants for the control of sintering/creep, Fast firing method, Two-step sintering method, Sintering of thin films. (4 hrs)

Course Objective

1 .

To provide an in-depth understanding of the basic atomistic phenomena that lead to high temperature processes of ceramics in particular and solids in generals.
2 .

To familiarize students with various types of sintering mechanisms and their applicability in different types of materials fabricated through powder metallurgy route.
3 .

To provide basic ideas of microstructure control during high temperature fabrication and service environment in ceramic materials.
4 .

To provide fundamental aspects of grain growth in dense materials and their control in ceramics and composites.

Course Outcome

1 .

Ability to apply basic physico-chemical principles to understand high temperature processes in materials in general, and ceramics in particular.
2 .

Ability to formulate processing methods for the sintering of single and multi-component ceramic materials.
3 .

Ability to comprehend materials microstructures and apply the knowledge in the problem solving of materials fabrication and performance in ceramic industries.
4 .

Ability to design microstructures for coarsening-resistant and creep-resistant alloys and composites.

Essential Reading

1 .

Suk-Joong L. Kang, Sintering: Densification, Grain Growth and Microstructure, Butterworth-Heinmann

2 .

M. N. Rahaman, Sintering of Ceramics, ., CRC Press, 2008

Supplementary Reading

1 .

D.W. Richerson, Modern Ceramic Engineering: Properties, Processing, and Use in Design, 3rd Ed,, CRC Press, 2006.

2 .

P. G. Shewmon, Diffusion in Solids, McGraw Hill, NY, 2nd edition, February 1998.

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE4101 : Power System Protection { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Over view of Power System Protection: General architecture of protection system, Evolution of relays, Attributes of a protection system, Current and potential transformer for relays, Zones of protections, Concept of primary and back-up protection.
(Hours: 3)
Module 2: Overcurrent Protection: Construction, Operating Principle and Characteristics of Instantaneous overcurrent relay, Definite Time overcurrent relay, Inverse Time overcurrent relay, Inverse definite minimum time overcurrent relay Co-ordination of overcurrent relays for radial lines, Overcurrent protection of three-phase feeder Construction, Operating Principle and Characteristics of Directional overcurrent relay, Directional overcurrent protection of a three-phase feeders Drawbacks of over current protection. (Hours: 7)
Module 3: Distance Protection: Universal Torque Equation, Construction, Operating Principle and Characteristics of Simple Impedance relay, Reactance relay, and Mho relay, performance of different impedance relays during normal loading condition, power swing and effect of arc resistance, Directional properties of various impedance relays, Impact of infeed effect Distance protection of a three-phase line, Three-stepped distance protection. (Hours: 6)
Module 4: Differential Protection: Dot convention, Simple differential protection–behavior during normal load, external fault and internal fault Actual behavior of a simple differential protection scheme and Percentage Differential relay. (Hours: 3)
Module 5: Busbar Protection: Differential protection of busbars, actual behavior of a protective current transformer – effect of CT saturation, High Impedance busbar protection. (Hours: 2)
Module 6: Transformer Protection: Over-current protection, Percentage differential protection of transformer, Inrush phenomenon, percentage differential relay with harmonic restraint, High resistance ground fault protection of a Y-? transformer, Inter-turn faults in transformer, Buchholz relay Protection against over-fluxing. (Hours: 5)
Module 7: Digital Relay: Architecture of a digital relay, Phasor Measurement technique, Numerical distance protection of transmission line, Elimination of decaying dc component, Distance protection by differential protection method, protection of transformer. (Hours: 5)
Module 8: Circuit Breaker: Requirement of circuit breakers, Characteristics of electric arc, Principle of A.C. and D.C. arc interruption, recovery and Restriking voltage and effect of current asymmetry upon them, Interruption of capacitive currents Various types of circuit breakers - Air-breaker circuit breaker, bulk-oil circuit breaker and minimum oil circuit breaker, Air-blast circuit breaker, SF_6 circuit breaker, Vacuum circuit breaker. (Hours: 5)

Course Objective

1 .

1. To understand the construction, working principle and application of electromechanical overcurrent protection.
2. To understand the basics of distance protection and its application.
3. To understand the logic behind differential protection and its application for transformers and bus bars protection.
4. To understand the need of digital relaying, its basic components and principles.
5. To understand the arc quenching mechanism in circuit breakers

Course Outcome

1 .

At the completion of the course, students will be able to
1. Design overcurrent protection for different elements of power system.
2. Implement different distance protection scheme for transmission line.
3. Design protection measure to entire power system with coordination among the relays placed at different location.
4. Design differential protection for transformer and Busbar.
5. Compare and design the electromagnetic and digital relays
6. Analyse the quenching mechanisms used in air, oil, vacuum and SF6 circuit breakers

S. S. Rao, Switch Gear and Protection, Khanna Publishers

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH6120 : Particle Physics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Elementary Particles, Particle Zoo and Four Interactions. Natural Units and relativity: four vector formalism. Klein-Gordon equation, Dirac equation and solutions. Lorentz covariance, C, P and T properties, bilinear covariants. Classical Field theory, Klein-Gordon and Dirac Lagrangian density. U(1) gauge theory, Noether's theorem. Canonical quantization of free scalar, spinor vector fields. QED, Dyson formalism, S matrix and Feynman rules. Basic QED processes: Mott scattering, Compton effect, etc. Yukawa theory: pion exchange potential and pion discovery. Fermi Theory of beta decay, Gamow-Teller correction. Introduction to groups, Lie groups, SU(3) and the eightfold way. Quark model, notion of colour. Parity violation. muon and pion decay. Non-Abelian gauge theories: SU(2) and SU(3) gauge theories. Spontaneous symmetry-breaking and gauge theory. Construction of electroweak model with one generation.

Course Objective

1 .

Understanding the mathematical formulation of physical phenomena that take place among elementary particles.
2 .

Understanding the application of group theory in Particle Physics.

Course Outcome

1 .

The students shall learn technical aspects of working in Particle Physics.
